name: Serpentfolk, Ascendant
body:
Ascendant Serpentfolk
CR 8

This tall ophidian has beautiful, glistening scales and exudes an imperious aura, though monstrous muscles coiling under its thick skin betray him as a deadly combatant.

XP 4,800
NE Medium monstrous humanoid
Init +10; Senses darkvision 60 ft., scent; Perception +18

DEFENSE

AC 25, touch 17, flat-footed 18 (+6 Dex, +1 dodge, +8 natural)
hp 94 (9d10+45)
Fort +7, Ref +12, Will +10
Immune mind-affecting effects, poison, paralysis; SR 19

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee +1 spear +17/+12 (1d8+10), bite +10 (1d6+3 plus poison)
Psychic Magic (CL 9th; concentration +14)

18 PE—anticipate thoughts (2 PE, DC 17), blur (2 PE), call spirit (5 PE, DC 20), command (1 PE, DC 16), disguise self (1 PE, DC 16), hypnotism (1 PE, DC 16), instigate psychic duel (2 PE, DC 17), mirror image (2 PE), suggestion (2 PE, DC 17), synesthesia (3 PE, DC 18)

STATISTICS

Str 22, Dex 23, Con 19, Int 18, Wis 15, Cha 20
Base Atk +9; CMB +15; CMD 32
Feats Dodge, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Power Attack, Toughness
Skills Acrobatics +15, Bluff +8, Escape Artist +17, Intimidate +11 Knowledge (arcana) +13, Perception +18, Sense Motive +11, Spellcraft +13, Stealth +18, Use Magic Device +18; Racial Modifiers +8 Escape Artist, +4 Perception, +4 Use Magic Device
Languages Aklo, Common, Draconic, Undercommon; telepathy 100 ft.
SQ psychic subjugator

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 18; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d4 Str; cure 2 consecutive saves.

Psychic Subjugator (Su)

An ascendant serpentfolk can affect creatures normally immune to mind-affecting effects with its mind-affecting psychic magic.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (usually jungles or underground)
Organization solitary, pair, or cabal (3-6)
Treasure standard (+1 spear, other treasure)

While most serpentfolk look upon their degenerate cousins with disdain, nowhere is that truer than in reclaimers. Those serpentfolk, already paragons of their kind, see themselves as torchbearers for their race and either exterminate their savage kin on sight or capture them for experiments meaning to uplift them back into intelligence.

Although most of these experiments are failures, a different breakthrough has been made. While granting degenerate serpentfolk higher intelligence is an ongoing and mostly unsuccessful process, some reclaimers shunned by the others have succeeded in cleverly subverting the process. Through various ways of manipulation, these serpentfolk have managed to enhance their bodies in a way similar to the biology of their degenerate kind. Keeping their intellect intact, they have put on layers of monstrous muscle covered in thick scales on top of their normally lithe bodies. Moreover, the transformation somehow enhanced their already potent psychic abilities, almost like it was the frailness of the body that was limiting them. Tall, graceful, monstrously strong and wielding potent magic, the so-called ascendant serpentfolk may be the closest that the race got to their prime since the ancient times, maybe even outmatching the serpentfolk of old in some ways. While the ascendant serpentfolk are in all ways superior to their cousins, degenerate or otherwise, not many of their kin see this achievement as a good thing. Whether justifying their actions by calling their methods impure, painting them as betrayers of their race or driven by simple jealousy, many other groups of serpentfolk hunt those ascendant exemplars down. Of course, the ascendant serpentfolk respond in kind to such treachery, subduing or slaying every member of their race who doesn’t believe in their vision. They see themselves as the path forward, the undisputed champions of their race and the true inheritors of their civilization. While it is unknown if normal serpentfolk can be uplifted to such might or if they are even able to breed true between themselves, it is certain that the ascendant serpentfolk have not stopped the plans and experiments they had in motion since they were reclaimers, and instead use their newfound power and freshly inflated arrogance to leave hiding and push onward to conquest. They recruit or subjugate their own kin and enslave various other creatures as soldiers or fodder for experiments. Some are even emboldened enough by their successes that they decide to disregard ancient faiths and beliefs of their race, forgoing their traditional goals and ways of life for a path laid forward by their vision alone. After all, tradition has led them to ruin once and it might take a new, greater caste of serpentfolk to decide what is now right for the race’s future.

While for now very limited in numbers, ascendant serpentfolk are vicious fighters and able psychics, with a sharp mind and enough ambition to learn new abilities quickly as needed. For this reason, many ascendant serpentfolk have class levels in various classes. Most commonly they are either fighters inspired by generals of old, wizards making use of their vast intellect and penchant for arcane magic or psychics harnessing their innate abilities to ever greater heights. An average ascendant serpentfolk is 7 feet tall and weighs 550 pounds. 10

This creature is tall, lanky, hunched and boasts an oversized head. Its perceived danger grows when you notice cords of lean muscle moving under the bronze, reptilian skin. The creature hisses, baring its teeth and looks upon you with a predatory gaze.
